titulo: Glasswing overwhelms maintainers with underwhelming findings (VulnCheck)
resumo: Patrick Garrity of VulnCheck has written a blog post that looks at vulnerabilities found by Anthropic's Project Glasswing since it launched on April 7, and finds it wanting: Of the 37,966 findings Anthropic reports, only 7,349 (19.4%) have been made public. Just 217 of those have been marked fixed. The more glaring number is that 4.4% (1,654) of the project's findings have already been marked as duplicates, 7.5x more duplicates than fixes. On top of that, 419 findings have been withdrawn. It seems odd that the ledger now claims a 94.2% true positive rate, up from 90.8% at launch, when more findings have been withdrawn or marked as duplicates than fixed, likely a feedback loop missing to the triage rates listed as "True Positives". [...] AI is a valuable tool for finding vulnerabilities, and I'm not discounting that. But seven months in, the evidence still doesn't match the launch narrative. The CVEs are a sliver of this year's total, almost none are being exploited, fixes have stalled while duplicates and withdrawals pile up, and the triage burden is shifting onto the open source maintainers Glasswing promised to help. The receipts keep coming in. They still don't reconcile.

titulo: How a warming ocean is changing the base of the marine food web
resumo: Climate change is causing warming in the oceans, which can have significant effects on marine food webs. Rising ocean temperatures can intensify seawater stratification, a process in which ocean water forms layers of different densities that mix less readily. This can reduce the supply of nutrients to surface waters and favor smaller phytoplankton species that are better adapted to low-nutrient conditions. Phytoplankton support zooplankton, which in turn transfer energy to fish and other animals. Changes in phytoplankton communities can therefore lead to cascading effects on marine food webs.

titulo: Why Nvidia can’t simply make more GeForce cards — even if it wants to

Nvidia designs its chips, but TSMC manufactures most of the silicon, while companies like SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron supply memory. Nvidia’s AI accelerators typically rely on high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and sophisticated packaging, while GeForce cards use consumer GPU-specific GDDR memory and different packaging. titulo: Microsoft just patched a serious Outlook flaw. Time to update!
resumo: Microsoft has issued an urgent warning regarding an actively exploited security flaw in Outlook. Designated as CVE-2026-124194 , the vulnerability enables attackers to trick users into opening a tampered message file. When opened, Outlook may connect to a server controlled by the attacker without displaying the usual security warning. This puts the user’s authentication credentials at risk of being leaked, which could lead to potential impersonation. Although Microsoft classifies the vulnerability as moderately severe, we recommend installing the latest security updates, as active exploitation has been confirmed. The affected products include Microsoft 365 for business, as well as Office LTSC 2021 and 2024. The user must open the malicious file themselves for the attack to succeed. The vulnerability is one of 1,093 that Microsoft addressed in its November security updates, according to the security firm Tenable . Of these, 63 are classified as critical.
